title: Flat morphisms and flat base change preserve maximal dominance
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\prime\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $h$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. A morphism is called maximally dominant if every generic point of an irreducible component of its source maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of its target [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then $h$ is maximally dominant. If $f$ is maximally dominant, the projection $X\times_Y Y\prime\to Y\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is maximally dominant. No finite-type, surjectivity, reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose II Example 1.1.3 and Proposition 1.1.5, printed p.23 (flat morphisms are generalizing and maximal dominance survives flat base change).
